judgments.catchwords: Contract Law — Agreement to Build and Rent — Manufacturing facility development on industrial land — Tenant’s premature termination of build-and-rent agreement — Failure to obtain planning permission (Kebenaran Merancang or KM Approval) within agreed timeline — Whether contractual deadline constituted essential condition — Waiver and election by conduct — Tenant’s continued affirmation of contract after expiry of deadline — Requirement to give reasonable notice to reinstate time as being of the essence — Whether termination valid — Whether termination amounted to repudiatory breach. Contract Law — Time of the Essence — Original deadline for obtaining planning permission not met — Contract affirmed after deadline — Whether fresh reasonable notice required before reliance on delay as ground for termination — Failure to reinstate time as being of the essence — Validity of termination. Contract Law — Repudiation — Wrongful termination by tenant — Landlord’s rejection of repudiation pursuant to s 40 Contracts Act 1950 — Whether agreement remained valid and subsisting — Attribution of responsibility for project failure. Contract Law — Variation Works — Additional construction works requested by tenant — Pits and trenches — Agreed additional costs — Partial payment made — Outstanding balance unpaid — Whether liability to pay survived subsequent contractual dispute. Restitution — Total Failure of Consideration — Claim for recovery of rental deposit and monies paid for variation works — Whether consideration wholly failed — Substantial performance of agreed works — Whether restitutionary claim sustainable. Guarantee and Indemnity — Construction of instrument — Guarantee securing tenant’s obligations under build-and-rent arrangement — Whether liability confined to tenancy period — Meaning of “Outstanding Sum” and agreed liquidated damages — Distinction between guarantee and indemnity under Contracts Act 1950 — Scope of indemnifier’s primary obligation. Guarantee and Indemnity — Enforcement against guarantor/indemnifier — Premature termination by principal debt

judgments.catchwords: 1. LAND LAW Compulsory acquisition — Land Acquisition Act 1960, ss. 4, 8, 14, 22 — Statutory procedure — Mandatory compliance — Alleged 1968 acquisition — Total failure to produce statutory notices, gazette declarations (Form D), valuation awards (Form G), or notice of possession (Form K) — Effect of non-compliance — Whether acquisition invalid and void ab initio. Indefeasibility of title — National Land Code, s. 89 — Register Document of Title (RDT) as conclusive evidence of title — Torrens system — Unendorsed 1968 acquisition — Certified Plan (PA/CP) — Whether cartographic measurements or survey plans confer title or validate compulsory taking in absence of registered Form K. Adverse possession — National Land Code, s. 341 — Limitation Act 1953, s. 9(2)(b) — Whether long physical occupation by public authority can defeat registered title or bar action for recovery. 2. TORT Trespass to land — Continuing trespass — Unauthorized construction and public operation of carriageway across private land — Cause of action arising de die in diem — Distinction between completed trespass and continuing trespass. Defences — Acquiescence — Tacit or implied consent — Requirement of positive acts or active encouragement from registered proprietor — Failure to plead defence in cause papers — Effect of long silence without positive encouraging acts. 3. CONSTITUTIONAL LAW Right to property — Federal Constitution, art. 13 — Compulsory acquisition of land without adequate compensation — Deprivation of property not in accordance with law — Article 13 guarantees. 4. PUBLIC AUTHORITIES & GOVERNMENT PROCEEDINGS Limitation of action — Public Authorities Protection Act 1948, s. 2(a) — Continuing injury or wrong — Whether limitation period begins to run while unauthorized physical occupation continues. Government liability — Government Proceedings Act 1956, ss. 5, 6 — Tortious entry committed prior to establishment of local authority (DBKL) — Vicarious and direct liability of Public Works Department (JKR), Director of Lands and Mines (PTG), and Federal Government. Public records — Loss of administrative files / institutional amnesia — Whether State can rely on passage of time or missing files to excuse non-production of statutory acquisition records. 5. REMEDIES & DAMAGES Equitable damages in lieu of injunction — Courts of Judicature Act 1964, Sched. para. 10 — Permanent public infrastructure on private land — Measure of damages based on open market value of encroached land. Co-owners / Co-proprietors — Undivided shares — Action instituted by two of three co-proprietors — Apportionment of market value damages matching proportionate undivided share (2/3 share). 6. EVIDENCE Expert evidence — Valuation report — Open market value of land — Failure of defendant to adduce counter-valuation report or expert evidence in rebuttal — Duty of court to accept uncontradicted expert opinion. Burden of proof — Evidence Act 1950 — Burden resting on acquiring authority to prove perfection of compulsory acquisition and payment of compensation.
